correctness.rationale: The source supplies the unitary moment-space model, proves a nonzero synthesis kernel, and gives its exact zero-set description after the atomic reduction. Outer-radius normalization gives m_{n+1} <= m_n, hence multiplication by z is contractive on the analytic moment space and preserves the kernel. Powers of any nonzero analytic kernel element are linearly independent, and their coefficient supports begin arbitrarily late. The unitary coefficient map identifies this kernel with the original frame synthesis kernel. No finite computation is used for an infinite claim.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These broader redundancy theorems act on sequences of the form A^n f_i with a fixed operator A. The normalized sequence T^n g/||T^n g|| generally cannot be written as powers of one fixed operator, so the cited power-stability and Carleson subsampling results do not cover the accepted claim. Conversely, the accepted claim does not assert their stronger deletion or subsampling conclusions.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper establishes the new possibility of normalized normal orbit frames and explicitly situates the problem beside recent redundancy work on Carleson frames. Upgrading the source's single dependence to infinite excess for every such normalized frame is a structural restriction, not a parameter tweak: it rules out all finite-excess normalized normal orbit frames and exhibits nontrivial coefficient relations arbitrarily far into the orbit. The mechanism is distinct from the power-subsampling arguments used for unnormalized positive operators.
